A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeMo-map research, with matching authors, core methodology and retained experiments. All pages, equations, tables and figures were readable, including v2's Appendices A–E; v1 has no appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original ATC experiments measuring motion-model accuracy, training and inference times, and alternative temporal encodings in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains the ATC experiments and adds ETH/UCY evaluation, quantitative trajectory-prediction results, and hyperparameter experiments in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Temporal input is broadened from periodic time-of-day to general continuous time. Appendix C uses frame indices for nonperiodic ETH/UCY sequences while retaining time-of-day for ATC. The spatial-grid/SIREN architecture, SWGMM outputs and negative-log-likelihood training remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates NeMo-map on indoor ATC motion mapping. v2 adds outdoor ETH, HOTEL, UNIV and ZARA scenes, including nonperiodic temporal variation, and directly evaluates NeMo-map in long-term trajectory prediction on ATC. This substantially expands both environmental and task coverage.

E2.justification: The mapping comparators remain CLiFF-map, Online CLiFF-map and STeF-map. v2 adds quantitative NeMo prediction comparisons against CLiFF-LHMP, STeF-LHMP, TUTR and MID in Table 4. Some predictors already appeared in v1's illustrative Figure 1; its Social LSTM comparator is omitted from v2's revised example.

E3.justification: The existing ATC mapping split, sampling rate and training settings are retained. The new prediction protocol uses 3-second observations, 10–60-second horizons, five predicted trajectories and ADE/FDE, selecting the most likely trajectory where available and averaging MID predictions. Appendix E additionally varies mixture count and spatial-grid resolution.

E4.justification: The temporal-encoding ablation is retained unchanged. Appendix E adds sensitivity studies of SWGMM component count and spatial-grid resolution. Figures 3–5 introduce comparative crossing-flow and changing-flow case studies, including spatial NLL heatmaps that expose baseline representation failures beyond v1's whole-map visualization.

E5.justification: Both versions use means, standard deviations, paired t-tests and 95% confidence intervals for NLL comparisons. v2 applies the existing standard-deviation and paired-test practices to prediction errors. Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, and no new uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: v1 Tables 1–3 are numerically retained as v2 Tables 1, 3 and 5. New results include four-scene ETH/UCY NLLs and 60-second prediction mean ADE/FDE of 5.08/10.97, versus 5.45/11.45 for CLiFF-LHMP (Table 4). Figures 3–8 add qualitative findings, horizon-dependent errors and hyperparameter trends.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 replaces normalized time-of-day t in [0,1] and the stated daily-periodicity assumption with a general continuous temporal variable t in R. The SWGMM definitions, parameter constraints and likelihood objective are retained; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion add a claim of demonstrated downstream trajectory-prediction performance, extending v1's mapping-focused contribution and proposed downstream usefulness. The introduction also replaces its specific nearly-two-orders-of-magnitude speedup claim with broader computational-efficiency language. The central continuous-MoD novelty claim remains.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits applicability to abrupt spatial or temporal changes, such as temporary barriers, and states that adaptation requires additional observations. It also interprets the new ablations as accuracy–resource tradeoffs and links prediction gains to continuous motion fields. The existing continuity and topology explanations remain.

D1.justification: Most implementation details move unchanged from Section 4.3 to Appendix C. v2 adds dataset-specific time preprocessing and prediction implementation details. Section 7 newly states that supplementary code, instructions, visualization scripts and per-sample NLL results are provided; their actual availability cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds the ETH/UCY dataset references by Pellegrini et al. (2009) and Lerner et al. (2007), removes Alahi et al. (2016), and expands descriptions of the already-cited TUTR and MID predictors. Its positioning against discretized MoDs and its distinction between motion priors and trajectory predictors remain.

P1.justification: v2 adds NeMo-map to the title and a publication header, shortens introductory prose, and rewrites the qualitative discussion. Dataset and implementation sections move to Appendices B/C, with new validation and disclosure sections added. The main section sequence and most methodological exposition are retained.

P2.justification: v1's whole-map all-component/dominant-component panels are replaced by extensive comparative flow and NLL-heatmap displays. v2 adds ETH/UCY and prediction tables, horizon plots and hyperparameter plots. The ATC layout moves to Appendix Figure 7, while the original planning illustration is removed and the trajectory illustration is revised.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's single-environment mapping study and illustrative downstream motivation: it directly tests additional environments and NeMo-guided trajectory prediction, examines spatial errors and parameter sensitivity, and states concrete failure conditions. ETH/UCY splits and the trajectory-generation procedure remain insufficiently specified, but the added evidence materially improves support for the method's applicability and usefulness.
